## What is Vaultwarden?

Vaultwarden is a Rust reimplementation of the Bitwarden server that's compatible with all official Bitwarden clients. It re-implements the Bitwarden server API in Rust and speaks the same protocol as bitwarden.com, so every official client works against it unchanged, but it fits in about 100 MB of RAM instead of the multi-container official stack.

## Key Benefits

- Your encrypted vault lives on your server, under your control. No third party has access to your data, your metadata, or your encryption keys

## VPS Requirements

Vaultwarden is extremely lightweight, so a Cloud VPS with 1 vCPU / 1GB RAM is more than enough. You'll need a domain name (e.g., vault.yourdomain.com) with a DNS A record pointing to your VPS and Nginx for reverse proxying — HTTPS is mandatory.

## Cost

For small teams and technical individuals, Vaultwarden's value proposition in 2026 is hard to beat: the full Bitwarden experience including organizations, advanced 2FA, and Send — running on a $5/month VPS, fully under your control, with zero per-seat licensing.

Based on the search results, here are the key differences between these three hosting types:

## Shared Hosting

Shared hosting places your website on a server along with hundreds, if not thousands, of other websites. While shared hosting users share the total amount of a single server's resources, VPS users benefit from dedicated portions of these resources. Shared hosting solutions are typically cheaper than their VPS counterparts, though you don't get the same level of server access, performance, or security.

## VPS Hosting

VPS hosting uses virtualization technology to divide a single physical server into multiple smaller "virtual" servers, with each virtual server operating independently and having its own allocated resources like CPU, RAM, and storage. VPS solutions provide greater access to server resources than shared hosting, delivering better performance with decreased loading times and improved bandwidth.

## Cloud Hosting

Cloud hosting services leverage a network of interconnected servers to host your website, with your data distributed across multiple servers in a "cloud," so if one cloud server fails, others pick up the slack. Cloud hosting is more scalable, flexible, and reliable, while VPS hosting is better suited for stable, smaller websites.

## Performance & Use Cases

Cloud hosting is significantly faster than shared hosting, and while both leverage a shared pool of resources, those in the cloud aren't tied to specific physical hardware and can be scaled up on-demand. Cloud hosting is ideal for large businesses, SaaS platforms, and eCommerce stores.

A VPS uses virtualization technology to divide a physical server into multiple virtual environments, with each VPS operating independently with its own dedicated resources, operating system, and software configuration.
